content.user_title: Organize Files With Safer Cleanup Plans
content.value_statement: Messy folders make files hard to find and duplicate cleanup risky. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through folder analysis, cleanup planning, and user-approved file moves.
actual_capabilities: Reviews a target directory and summarizes file types, sizes, and obvious organization issues.
Groups files by type, purpose, project, date, or archive status.
Finds exact duplicate candidates and similar names before recommending what to keep.
Builds a proposed folder structure with files that need user decisions.
Creates folders, moves files, and renames files after explicit approval.
Provides a cleanup summary and maintenance habits for future organization.
limitations: It depends on local command availability, such as find, du, file, and md5.
It cannot judge sensitive files safely without user-provided boundaries.
It should not delete files without a reviewed plan and explicit confirmation.
It may need platform-specific command changes on Windows or restricted systems.

use_cases.title: Clean A Downloads Folder
use_cases.description: Sort documents, images, installers, archives, and uncertain items into a clear review plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Archives
use_cases.description: Separate completed work, active files, references, and old versions before archiving a project.

use_cases.title: Review Duplicate Candidates
use_cases.description: Compare duplicate candidates by path, size, date, and name before choosing what to keep.

prompt_templates.title: Organize My Downloads
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the file-organizer skill on my Downloads folder. First show the current state and ask before moving or deleting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Find Duplicate Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this folder for duplicate candidates. Show exact paths, sizes, dates, and your recommendation before I approve any deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Project Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this messy project directory and propose a cleaner folder structure. Separate active work, references, archives, and files that need my decision.

prompt_templates.title: Create And Execute A Safe Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this directory, produce a step-by-step migration plan, include an undo log format, and execute only the actions I approve.

output_examples.input: A user asks to organize a cluttered Downloads folder.
output: Current state summary with file counts, top file types, large files, and likely clutter.
Proposed folders for documents, images, archives, installers, and items needing review.
Approval request before any move, rename, or deletion.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether duplicate files can be removed.
output: Groups likely duplicates by hash or similar name.
Shows path, size, and date for each candidate.
Recommends which file to keep and asks for confirmation before deletion.

output_examples.input: A user asks to archive an old project.
output: Separates active files, completed work, references, and uncertain items.
Suggests archive folders and naming rules.
Summarizes completed moves and future maintenance steps.

best_practices: Start with one directory and define files or folders that are out of scope.
Review the proposed plan before allowing moves, renames, or deletion.
Keep an undo log of every change made during cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not run cleanup across an entire home folder without clear boundaries.
Do not delete duplicate candidates based only on matching names.
Do not move active project files before confirming ownership and current use.

faq.question: Can this skill delete files?
faq.answer: It can recommend deletion for duplicates or trash, but it should ask for explicit confirmation before deleting anything.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows that can inspect local files.

faq.question: Will it organize my whole computer automatically?
faq.answer: No. It should work on a defined directory and ask before broad or destructive changes.

faq.question: Can it find duplicate files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest hash, name, size, and date checks, then show candidates for review.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Choose a target folder, list protected folders, and decide how conservative the cleanup should be.

faq.question: Does it support Windows?
faq.answer: The guidance is general, but some sample commands may need Windows equivalents.
